key: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra’s helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
s: In a hymn on Indra’s fight with Vrtra, the verse turns to the praise and the Maruts; Sāyaṇa, on 1.52.9, reads the ‘lofty’ hymn as the Bṛhat Sāman, sung in fear of Vrtra, and the Maruts as serving men in the form of breath.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.52.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 237934 (2020)

evidence.gloss: ‘Bṛhat’ is the Bṛhat Sāman: when the praisers, the sacrificers, through fear, fear of Vṛtra, made it a hymn fit for praise … the sense is that, afraid of Vṛtra, they praised Indra with such a hymn … nṛṣācaḥ: becoming servers of men in the form of breath, (the Maruts) in that same form gladdened Indra too, one after another.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.52.9, at [51,9]), the whole verse, no dash. Sāyaṇa on 1.52.9 glosses bṛhat as bṛhatsāma, sung by the praisers bhiyasā vṛtrabhayena (in fear of Vṛtra), and nṛṣācaḥ as prāṇarūpeṇa nṝn sevamānāḥ (serving men in the form of breath); Wilson’s note a confirms ‘the Scholiast adds Sama’. The reading adds nothing beyond these words. Plain sense: hymn 1.52 is Indra’s fight with Vrtra (vv. 2, 5, 6, 8, 10, 15) and the verse speaks of the hymn and the Maruts; no four words of the key; faithful. Revision 237934 is dated 2020-05-14 by the Wikisource API, so the src year stands. Yāska does not treat this hymn. Evidence pieces re-found by machine in the packet. entry-check ok.
